scope.focus: Project Engine autonomy lineage: project-local workspace -> sandboxed tool agent -> full-system authority widening -> tiered autonomous project engine -> replay/policy/A-B/multi-project coordination

lineage.event: Introduced a per-project workspace explicitly framed as Claude with Frank peripherals rather than Frank itself: project folder, project-local persistent memory, project-local hypotheses, chat history and CRUD/API surfaces. This is an early explicit identity/module boundary precedent.

Converted the workspace into a tool-using coding agent with bash/read/write/edit/list operations, a bounded 15-iteration tool loop, project-root path confinement, destructive-command filtering and exact-string edit semantics that fail on zero or multiple matches instead of silently mutating ambiguous text.

Removed project-folder confinement and widened the same agent to full-system filesystem, service, package-manager and shell authority while shrinking the destructive-command blocklist. This is a historical authority-boundary transition, not evidence that unrestricted authority is desirable.

Rebuilt Project Engine into a goal-driven autonomous platform with tiered decision routing, action chaining, persistent goals, an entity-relation world model, evolving agent profile, hard/soft policy engine, tool-outcome learning, heartbeat/checkpoint recovery and low-cost/free-model delegation. Commit-reported demonstrations included a 39 s zero-Claude-token autonomy cycle, a five-step autonomous chain and a real project contacting dealers.

Added smart notifications, natural-language policy parsing, profile cloning, A/B strategy testing, peer-project queries, session replay/time-travel and a manual autonomy trigger. The implementation records useful observability surfaces but also exposes several important historical counterexamples for modern authority/evidence design.

mechanism_findings.finding: Persistent agentic project work was already separated into goal state, project memory, hypotheses, world model, profile, policies, action traces and checkpoints rather than one undifferentiated chat transcript.
The architecture used explicit cost/latency tiers before invoking expensive cognition, demonstrating an early routing pattern analogous to current Needle/model-routing goals.
Replay/time-travel, activity feeds and checkpoints were treated as first-class agent-operability features before current Harness/UnifiedDB formalization.
Exact-edit failure on ambiguous matches is a reusable historical safety pattern: mutation should fail closed when the intended target is not uniquely identified.

negative_results_and_counterexamples.result: The project-root sandbox was later removed and replaced with nearly unrestricted full-system authority plus a very small command blocklist.
negative_results_and_counterexamples.impact: This lineage demonstrates that convenience can erase a previously explicit capability boundary. Current Clay/FRANK should preserve external capability authorization, scoped effects and receipts rather than relying on prompt intent or a blacklist.

negative_results_and_counterexamples.result: The v3.2 A/B test scores a strategy primarily by whether autonomous action text contains [ERROR] or [TIMEOUT], then automatically writes the apparent winner into goal strategy state.
negative_results_and_counterexamples.impact: Execution success is not task success. Modern experiment selection must score causal/outcome receipts and preserve uncertainty instead of treating absence of tool errors as strategy quality.

negative_results_and_counterexamples.result: Natural-language policy text is converted by a free LLM into JSON and then persisted as a policy after syntactic extraction, with no independently evidenced formal semantic validation step in the inspected change.
negative_results_and_counterexamples.impact: User-language intent parsing must remain separate from enforcement authority; hard policy activation needs deterministic validation, provenance and reversible confirmation semantics.

negative_results_and_counterexamples.result: The manual autonomy endpoint starts a daemon thread and immediately returns that the cycle started; the shown path logs failures but does not itself prove durable started/completed/effect receipts.
negative_results_and_counterexamples.impact: Queued/started/done/effect states must remain distinct. Harness and Dynamic Work should require durable lifecycle receipts rather than HTTP acknowledgement as completion evidence.

negative_results_and_counterexamples.result: Agent profile cloning copies strengths, weaknesses, tool preferences and learned rules across projects as a bulk profile transfer.
negative_results_and_counterexamples.impact: Cross-context learned behavior needs provenance, compatibility and context validity checks; transfer itself does not establish that a learned rule remains correct in the target project.

current_inheritance.delta: Preserve the historical decomposition into goal, task/action trace, tool effect, checkpoint and replay, but strengthen it to durable queued->claimed->started->effect->verified lifecycle receipts. HTTP/tool success alone is never completion.

Retain the tiered-decision principle: use deterministic/code paths and cheaper cognition where evidence says they suffice, escalate only when uncertainty/complexity justifies it, and measure routing quality against outcome not cost alone.

Represent capability scope, policy provenance, action intent, target identity, preconditions, effect receipt, outcome receipt and rollback as typed execution contracts. Exact/unique target resolution should be a first-class mutation precondition.

Historical project state argues for logically unified but typed storage of goals, policies, world-model entities, memories, strategy trials, notifications, checkpoints and replay events with explicit project/context identity and transfer provenance.
The historical entity-relation world model and peer-project query are useful precursors, but cross-project association must not imply cross-project policy validity or execution authority.

Reject the historical unrestricted full-system authority pattern as a default. Use external capability/commit gateways, least-necessary scope, deterministic validation for enforcement changes and receipt-backed effects.
The A/B lineage is a concrete anti-Goodhart lesson: discriminate hypotheses/strategies using outcome-grounded tests and falsifiers, not absence of runtime errors or worker agreement.

cheap_discriminating_tests: Run the same edit request against zero, one and two matching targets; only the unique target may mutate and every attempt must leave a receipt.
Run paired strategies where both tools exit successfully but only one improves the task metric; the experiment framework must select by outcome metric rather than error absence.
Feed an ambiguous natural-language hard policy and require parse->deterministic validation->human/authority acceptance separation before enforcement state changes.
Trigger an asynchronous action that crashes after acknowledgement and assert started, failed and effect states remain distinguishable after restart/replay.
Transfer a learned rule between two intentionally incompatible project contexts and require compatibility/provenance gating to reject or quarantine it.
Compare unrestricted-system-agent execution with scoped capability tokens on the same benchmark; measure success, unauthorized reachable surface, rollback completeness and receipt fidelity.

earned_work.reason: Historically reusable architecture and counterexample value is material, but exact reusable-hour credit requires row-level dedup against current Dynamic Work, Harness, Needle, UnifiedDB, security and replay mappings.

level0_effect.reason: Completed one additional semantic/history lineage shard. Project-Frankenstein repository-wide tree/history denominator remains unfrozen, so no exact global Level-0 coverage may be claimed.
